title: Intervention Counts for Recovering Latent DAG Mixtures under Size-Capped Experiments
banked_reason: kernel_substituted@oeq:universal-frontier — The headline all-parameter, evaluable universal-factor frontier remains explicitly to-prove; the delivered feasibility threshold, cover upper bound, and supported slices are a strictly weaker kernel.
gap_reasons: The headline all-parameter, evaluable universal-factor frontier remains explicitly to-prove; the delivered feasibility threshold, cover upper bound, and supported slices are a strictly weaker kernel.
The all-parameter constant-factor frontier and general structured-class formulas remain open.
The load-bearing all-parameter step remains coexistence of blocker requirements on one legal baseline transcript.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery established the exact intervention-size feasibility boundary, a parent-blocking cover upper bound, legal full-oracle transcript and faithful-realization tools, and three exact supported slices. The matching all-parameter adaptive converse collapsed because the blocker requirements could not be made to coexist on one legal capped baseline; consequently the promised universal frontier and general tree/cycle-free formulas remain open.
tldr: The paper studies the experiment-count cost of oriented-union recovery for latent DAG mixtures under size-capped interventions. It proves the exact finite-versus-infinite panel-size boundary, an explicit parent-blocking cover upper bound, legal full-oracle transcript tools, faithful lower-witness realizations, and exact counts on three supported slices; the all-parameter constant-factor frontier and general structured-class formulas remain open.
gap: Varıcı et al. identify worst-case local intervention sizes and give a quadratic-count algorithm, but explicitly leave bounded-size intervention-count lower bounds open. Single-DAG count arguments condition on a known skeleton or essential graph and therefore do not control emergent nonedges or selector-induced ancestor cycles.
fill: The project derives a descendant-signature representation of the hard oracle subclass, proves the exact feasibility boundary, builds an explicit parent-blocking cover, and resolves the remaining gap through a legal blocker-packing benchmark that yields matching universal-factor bounds and exact structured-class formulas.
